subject: Benchmark methodology & streaming SLO handoff - OmniShop
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Nora Lim <nora@omnishop.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: benchmark handoff and prompt provenance

Thanks again for your time this morning, Nora — good first pass on scope. Below is a concise post-call recap and the handoff items we need to run a meaningful baseline/qualification run for the OmniShop checkout flow. Please confirm or correct anything I missed.

Key goals (as we understood them)
- Validate streaming latency SLO for live item recommendations in checkout (interactive stream).
- Ensure p95/p99 latency targets for synchronous API paths (price lookup, promo tidy).
- Establish reproducible benchmark that Redwood and OmniShop can re-run for future model rollouts.

Initial SLO targets (proposed)
- Synchronous endpoints: p95 <= 250 ms, p99 <= 400 ms (95th/99th token completion latency).
- Streaming interactive flow: tail latency (first token) target <= 150 ms for cold-connection; steady-state tokens/sec measured separately.
- Throughput/concurrency: baseline target 500 sustained QPS across mixed traffic; streaming concurrency window ~80 simultaneous streams.

Handoff asks (what we need from OmniShop)
1) Prompt seed set: canonical prompts + expected golden outputs (10–50 canonical cases). Attach as a single JSON.
2) Traffic mix: percentage split between streaming vs sync calls, average tokens per call, expected peak concurrency windows.
3) Any tokenization/normalization rules you apply (custom stopwords, pre-processing).
4) Test account or synthetic traffic generator details + rate limits/credentials.
5) Security/compliance constraints for any test data (PII removal rules).

Attachments: see "omnishop_prompt_sample.json" placeholder attached to this message (seed prompts + expected labels).

Proposed next steps
- OmniShop: confirm prompt set and traffic mix by EOD Thu 2028-03-29.
- Redwood: provide benchmark template and measurement definitions (I’ll attach).
- Schedule: tentative run window 2028-04-04 to 2028-04-06 for baseline measurements.

If that schedule or the SLO targets look off to you, call it out and we’ll adjust.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Ava

From: Nora Lim <nora@omnishop.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Mike Dawson <mike.dawson@auditify.io>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: benchmark handoff and prompt provenance

Thanks, Ava — appreciate the succinct recap. A few clarifications and constraints from our side:

Clarifications
- The streaming flow is used for real-time upsell copy in checkout; we consider first token latency critical (we observe abandonment at ~400ms). Your 150ms first-token target is aggressive but aligns with product needs.
- For traffic mix: typical production is ~60% sync (price/promos) and 40% streaming (recommendations) during checkout surges. Peak concurrency last Black Friday was ~1.2k concurrent streams for 45s.

Security constraints
- All prompt/test inputs must have PII removed. We will provide synthetic-sensitive variants where needed. Auditify (cc’d) will validate the de-identification approach.

Deliverables timeline
- We’ll attach the prompt seed set by EOD Thu 2028-03-29 (omnishop_prompt_sample.json).
- We can provide a short read-only test account for benchmarking (API key with limited scope) by Monday 2028-04-01.

One ask: can you include in your measurement-defs.md how you measure streaming throughput (open streams vs tokens/sec) and how you handle client-lag in measurements? We want to ensure apples-to-apples with our client-side metrics.

— Nora
Director, Product — OmniShop

Attachment: omnishop_prompt_sample.json (JSON, 32 KB)
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Nora Lim <nora@omnishop.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: benchmark handoff and prompt provenance

Great, Nora — thanks for the context and the high-water mark number from last Black Friday. We’ll treat Black Friday as an upper-bound test case. A few items I’m attaching and calling out explicitly so there’s no ambiguity on how Redwood will run the baseline:

What Redwood will supply (attached)
- redwood_benchmark_template.yaml — harness config (workload mix, concurrency profile, tokenization hooks).
- measurement-defs.md — concrete definitions for latency/throughput/streaming metrics and reproducibility checklist.

How we measure streaming throughput and client lag (excerpt)
- Open streams: we measure concurrent open SSE/WebSocket connections maintained by the client; server-side concurrency is counted when the initial handshake is accepted.
- Tokens/sec steady-state: measured on the server by averaging generated tokens over a 30s steady-state window per stream; we report median and 90th percentile tokens/sec across streams.
- Client-lag handling: we timestamp outgoing request at client and incoming first-token at server; to map to client observed latency we will (optionally) provide server-side timestamp traces and a small client-side tracer script. If you’d like exact parity with your client metrics, we can ingest your tracer output.

Reproducibility notes
- Seed handling: we’ll run with deterministic random seeds and store the seed ID used for each trial in the harness output.
- Prompt normalization: we will canonicalize whitespace, lowercase comparisons for labels where you’ve indicated that’s acceptable, and we will not alter the prompt semantics.
- Golden outputs: where you provide an expected label, the harness will run exact-match and token-level similarity checks (edit distance and embedding similarity).

Proposed measurement window
- Run window: 2028-04-04 to 2028-04-06 (we’ll prioritize an early morning slot on 04-04 PST).
- We’ll provide a schedule for three runs: baseline (no caching), caching-enabled, and production-emulation (traffic spikes).

Attachments in this message: redwood_benchmark_template.yaml, measurement-defs.md (see drive link in metadata).

If that reads OK I’ll send a short playbook for on-call contacts during the run and open a read-only sandbox API key once you share the credentials.

Thanks,
Ava

Attachment: redwood_benchmark_template.yaml (YAML, 4 KB)
Attachment: measurement-defs.md (Markdown, 6 KB)
